what_happened: The operator ran the CI wiring request (job efyd) directly, ahead of Athena's plan. The CI routing is already built but does nothing, because candidates are never pushed to CI. The owner's top priority is speed through CI, and the plan would not rank this job first. No decision was matched.
cause: The plan orders work by default type and position. It takes no input from the owner's stated priority and does not check whether work already built is delivering value. CI routing items were planned as separate pieces, so the last piece (pushing candidates) fell back to its default place while the earlier pieces sat inert. The queue has no priority support, so the operator's only lever is to bypass the plan. Earlier bypasses were logged but never turned into a fix, so the pattern keeps recurring.
prevention: Add an owner-priority input to the plan and to the queue. The owner records an ordered priority list, such as speed via CI. The planner ranks any job tagged to a top priority ahead of default-ordered work, and keeps a multi-item series together until its end-to-end outcome works. The queue drain honors that priority. The plan also flags built-but-inert work, where a feature has landed but its trigger is not wired, and raises the job that activates it. Each plan run compares its order with the owner's latest priority and reports any difference.
proposed_request: Add owner-priority ordering to Athena's plan and queue. (1) Let the owner keep an ordered priority list in the repo, with the current top item being speed via CI. (2) Make the planner rank jobs tagged to a listed priority ahead of default type and position ordering, and keep all items of a series together until the series' end-to-end outcome works. (3) Make the queue drain take items by priority first and then oldest first. (4) Have each plan run report any place where its order differs from the owner's priority list, and flag features that have landed but are inert because nothing triggers them, such as CI routing with no candidate pushes. Acceptance: with CI wiring and a lower-priority job both queued, the plan and drain run CI wiring first without operator intervention, and a test shows this.
